questions.question: Padma Shri awardees in 2022, known for their great performances of the dance style of Kathak, sister duo Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana belong to which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana**, sister duo, are renowned for their contributions to the **Kathak dance form**.
 
• They were awarded the **Padma Shri** in 2022 for their exceptional performances and dedication to preserving Indian classical dance.
 
• The sisters hail from the state of **Uttar Pradesh**, which has a rich tradition in Kathak.
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight classical dance forms of India and is deeply rooted in the cultural heritage of northern India, including Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Their work emphasizes **traditional storytelling** through dance, blending rhythmic footwork, graceful movements, and intricate expressions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak**:

 
 
• Kathak is an ancient Indian classical dance form known for its storytelling aspects, deriving its name from the Sanskrit word **"Katha"**, meaning story.
 
• It is characterized by **fast footwork**, spins, and intricate gestures, accompanied by classical Hindustani music.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri Award**:
 
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in India, presented for distinguished contributions in various fields like arts, education, literature, sports, and social work.
 
• It is announced annually on **Republic Day** by the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Role of Uttar Pradesh in Kathak**:
 
 
• Uttar Pradesh is considered the **birthplace of Kathak**, especially the Lucknow Gharana, which is renowned for its focus on expressions and storytelling.
 
• Lucknow and Varanasi have historically been centers for the development and preservation of Kathak traditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Padma Shri Awardees (Dance in 2022)**:
 
 
• Other prominent dancers who received the Padma Shri in 2022 include **Dr. Sonal Mansingh** (Odissi) and **Ramli Ibrahim** (Bharatanatyam).

questions.question: How does flexibility of the cell membrane help living organisms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Absorbs food**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The flexibility of the cell membrane allows **cells to engulf nutrients** from their surroundings through a process called **endocytosis**.
 
• It enables the transport of essential molecules like glucose, amino acids, and ions into the cell, ensuring proper **cellular function**.
 
• The cell membrane’s dynamic nature supports **selective permeability**, allowing the absorption of beneficial substances while excluding harmful ones.
 
• This property helps cells in maintaining **homeostasis**, which is vital for their survival and function.
 
• Flexibility also aids in cellular communication by facilitating the interaction of membrane receptors with external signals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Membrane Structure:** The cell membrane is composed of a **phospholipid bilayer** with embedded proteins, making it semi-permeable and flexible.
 
• **Endocytosis:** A process where cells absorb external materials by engulfing them within vesicles formed from the cell membrane.
 
• **Selective Permeability:** The ability of the membrane to allow certain molecules to pass through while blocking others, crucial for nutrient absorption and waste removal.
 
• **Fluid Mosaic Model:** This model describes the cell membrane as a dynamic structure where lipids and proteins can move laterally, ensuring its flexibility and functionality.
 
• **Homeostasis:** The cell membrane plays a key role in maintaining the internal balance of the cell by regulating the exchange of substances with its environment.

questions.question: The five-year plan for 1956–1961 was prepared by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PC Mahalanobis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **PC Mahalanobis** was an Indian statistician and economist known for his contributions to India's economic planning.
 
• The second five-year plan (1956–1961) was based on the **Mahalanobis model**, which emphasized industrialization and heavy industries.
 
• This plan aimed to allocate resources to accelerate the economic growth of India by focusing on the **public sector** and reducing dependency on imports.
 
• PC Mahalanobis was the founder of the **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)** and introduced advanced statistical methods in economic planning.
 
• The Mahalanobis model was a cornerstone of India's economic planning during the early years post-independence, promoting a self-reliant economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India:**

 
 
• The five-year plans were introduced in India under the Planning Commission, inspired by the Soviet model.
 
• They aimed at achieving balanced economic growth and addressing key sectors like agriculture, industry, and infrastructure.
 
• The first five-year plan (1951–1956) focused on agricultural development and addressing food scarcity.
 
 
 
• **Mahalanobis Model:**
 
 
• The Mahalanobis model emphasized the growth of the heavy industry sector, considering it as the backbone of economic development.
 
• It proposed a two-sector model, dividing the economy into consumer goods and investment goods sectors.
 
• This model aimed to prioritize long-term growth by investing heavily in capital goods industries.
 
 
 
• **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI):**
 
 
• Founded by PC Mahalanobis in 1931, ISI contributed significantly to the development of statistics and economic planning in India.
 
• ISI is recognized globally for its research in statistics, operations research, and economics.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission:**
 
 
• Established in 1950, the Planning Commission was responsible for formulating India's five-year plans until it was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.
 
• It aimed to assess resources and prioritize development goals for India's socio-economic progress.

questions.question: Padma Bhushan awardee Lalgudi Gopala Jayaraman was associated with which of the following musical genres?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carnatic music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lalgudi Gopala Jayaraman** was a renowned violinist, composer, and exponent of **Carnatic music**, a classical music form of Southern India.
 
• He was born on **17 September 1930**, in Lalgudi, Tamil Nadu, into a family deeply rooted in Carnatic music traditions.
 
• He was known for pioneering the **Lalgudi Bani**, a unique style of violin playing that emphasizes melody and lyrical expression.
 
• In recognition of his immense contributions to Indian classical music, he was awarded the prestigious **Padma Bhushan** in 2001.
 
• His compositions include **varnams, kritis, and tillanas**, which are widely performed in the Carnatic music tradition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic Music:**

 
 
• Carnatic music is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Hindustani music.
 
• It originated in South India and is known for its intricate compositions and devotional themes.
 
• The key components of Carnatic music include **raga** (melodic framework) and **tala** (rhythmic cycle).
 
 
 
• **Violin in Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• The violin was introduced into Carnatic music in the early 19th century and is now a staple instrument in this tradition.
 
• It is played in a seated posture, with the instrument held horizontally and resting on the player’s ankle.
 
 
 
• **Lalgudi Bani:**
 
 
• Lalgudi Bani is the unique style of violin playing developed by Lalgudi Gopala Jayaraman.
 
• It emphasizes lyrical expression, tonal precision, and a seamless blend of melody and rhythm.
 
 
 
• **Padma Bhushan Award:**
 
 
• The Padma Bhushan is India’s third-highest civilian award, conferred for distinguished service of a high order in any field.
 
• Lalgudi Gopala Jayaraman received this honor in 2001 for his outstanding contributions to Carnatic music.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts added the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act**, enacted in **1976**.
 
• This amendment incorporated **Article 51A** under Part IV-A of the Constitution, outlining 10 Fundamental Duties for citizens.
 
• The amendment was introduced during the tenure of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi** as part of efforts to strengthen democracy.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union, aiming to promote responsible citizenship and national unity.
 
• The list of duties was later expanded to 11 by the **86th Amendment Act** in 2002, which added the duty to provide opportunities for education to children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced through courts.
 
• They serve as moral obligations for citizens to uphold the spirit of the Constitution and contribute to the nation.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act:**
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act is often referred to as the **"Mini Constitution"** because of the extensive changes it brought.
 
• It amended several articles, including the Preamble, and introduced concepts like the primacy of Directive Principles over Fundamental Rights.
 
 
 
• **Part IV-A of the Constitution:**
 
 
• Part IV-A was introduced solely to include Fundamental Duties.
 
• It emphasizes duties such as respecting the national symbols, safeguarding public property, and promoting harmony.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A:**
 
 
• Article 51A lists duties like abiding by the Constitution, protecting sovereignty, and preserving the environment.
 
• The duties are applicable to all citizens of India, irrespective of age or profession.

questions.question: Which of the statements is also known as the government budget?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annual Financial Statement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Annual Financial Statement** is a document presented by the government as part of the **Union Budget**, containing a summary of the government's revenue and expenditure for a financial year.
 
• It is mandated under **Article 112 of the Indian Constitution**, which requires the government to present the Union Budget annually.
 
• The Annual Financial Statement is divided into three parts: **Consolidated Fund of India**, **Contingency Fund of India**, and **Public Account of India**.
 
• This statement includes estimates of receipts and expenditures for the upcoming financial year, along with actuals from the previous year and revised estimates for the current year.
 
• The Union Finance Minister presents the Annual Financial Statement in Parliament, typically on February 1st.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Consolidated Fund of India:**

 
 
• It is the most important fund of the Government of India and includes all **revenues (taxes, non-taxes)**, **borrowings**, and **receipts of loans**.
 
• All government expenditures are made from this fund, subject to parliamentary approval.
 
 
 
• **Contingency Fund of India:**
 
 
• It is set up under Article 267 of the Constitution and is used to meet **urgent or unforeseen expenses**.
 
• The fund is placed at the disposal of the President of India, who authorizes withdrawals.
 
 
 
• **Public Account of India:**
 
 
• This account deals with funds received by the government in trust, such as provident funds, small savings, etc.
 
• These funds do not require parliamentary approval for withdrawal but are managed as per statutory provisions.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget:**
 
 
• The Union Budget is an annual financial statement that provides details of the government's plan for **revenue generation** and **expenditure allocation**.
 
• It includes two components: **Revenue Budget** (income and routine expenses) and **Capital Budget** (investments and long-term expenses).

questions.question: As per SRS Bulletin 2020, what was the death rate in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The death rate in India for the year 2020, as per the **Sample Registration System (SRS) Bulletin**, was reported to be **6 per 1,000 population**.
 
• The **death rate** is defined as the number of deaths occurring per 1,000 individuals in a given year.
 
• The SRS is the **primary source** for accurate and reliable annual estimates of birth rate, death rate, and other fertility and mortality indicators in India.
 
• India’s death rate has been steadily declining over the decades due to improved healthcare facilities, sanitation, and awareness of preventive health measures.
 
• The figures released by the SRS Bulletin are crucial for policy-making and monitoring the progress of health initiatives in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sample Registration System (SRS):**

 
 
• The SRS is a demographic survey conducted by the **Registrar General of India** to provide reliable annual estimates of demographic indicators.
 
• It was initiated in **1970** and is implemented in both rural and urban areas.
 
• The system captures data through continuous enumeration and six-monthly retrospective surveys.
 
 
 
• **Death Rate Trends in India:**
 
 
• India's death rate has significantly declined from **25 per 1,000 population in 1951** to **6 per 1,000 population in 2020**.
 
• This decline is attributed to advancements in medical technology, better healthcare infrastructure, and improved living standards.
 
 
 
• **Mortality Indicators:**
 
 
• Other mortality indicators include **infant mortality rate**, **maternal mortality rate**, and **age-specific mortality rates**.
 
• These indicators help assess the health status and performance of healthcare systems in the country.
 
 
 
• **Health Initiatives in India:**
 
 
• Government programs like **Ayushman Bharat**, **National Health Mission**, and **Janani Suraksha Yojana** aim to reduce mortality rates and improve public health.
 
• These initiatives focus on preventive healthcare, affordability, and accessibility for all citizens.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations was started by Pandita Ramabai Saraswati in 1882?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arya Mahila Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Arya Mahila Samaj** was founded by **Pandita Ramabai Saraswati** in **1882** in Pune, India.
 
• The organization aimed at promoting women’s education and addressing the social issues faced by Indian women, especially widows.
 
• Pandita Ramabai was a prominent social reformer, educationist, and advocate for women’s rights, particularly in the 19th-century Indian context.
 
• The Arya Mahila Samaj played a critical role in creating awareness about the need for women's empowerment and was a precursor to several women's rights movements in India.
 
• The institution also worked towards providing shelter and education to widows, as well as advocating for their remarriage, which was a taboo in Indian society at the time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandita Ramabai Saraswati**:

 
 
• She was one of the earliest champions of women's education and emancipation in India.
 
• Ramabai was the first Indian woman to be awarded the title of "Pandita" for her deep knowledge of Sanskrit scriptures.
 
 
 
• **Sharda Sadan (1889):**
 
 
• Pandita Ramabai also established the Sharda Sadan (House of Learning) in Bombay to educate widows and destitute women.
 
• It later became a significant institution contributing to women's education in India.
 
 
 
• **Women’s Education in 19th Century India:**
 
 
• Women’s education was largely neglected and opposed by conservative factions of society during this period.
 
• Reformers like Pandita Ramabai, Jyotirao Phule, and Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar were instrumental in advancing female literacy and empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj:**
 
 
• The Arya Mahila Samaj drew inspiration from the Arya Samaj movement founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati, which advocated for social reforms based on Vedic principles.

questions.question: What is a good indicator of economic growth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross Domestic Product**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** is the total monetary value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders over a specific time period, usually annually or quarterly.
 
• It is considered the most comprehensive measure of a country’s economic performance and growth.
 
• GDP reflects the overall economic activity, including consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports (exports minus imports).
 
• A higher GDP indicates a growing economy, while a declining GDP might signal an economic downturn or recession.
 
• Governments and policymakers use GDP as a critical indicator to formulate fiscal and monetary policies and evaluate the economic impact of various initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of GDP:**

 
 
• **Nominal GDP:** Measures the economic output using current market prices, without adjusting for inflation.
 
• **Real GDP:** Adjusts for inflation, providing a more accurate representation of an economy's growth over time.
 
• **GDP Per Capita:** Divides the GDP by the total population to measure the average economic output per person.
 
 
 
• **Components of GDP:**
 
 
• **Consumption:** Spending by households on goods and services.
 
• **Investment:** Expenditure on capital goods like machinery, buildings, and infrastructure.
 
• **Government Spending:** Expenditure by the government on public services and infrastructure.
 
• **Net Exports:** The value of exports minus the value of imports.
 
 
 
• **GDP Growth Rate:** Indicates how fast an economy is growing or contracting and is a critical measure of economic health.
 
• **Limitations of GDP:**
 
 
• Does not account for the distribution of income or economic inequality.
 
• Excludes non-market activities such as unpaid domestic work and volunteer services.
 
• Does not measure environmental sustainability or the well-being of citizens.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Indicators:** Other measures like Gross National Happiness (GNH) and Human Development Index (HDI) are sometimes used to complement GDP for a holistic view of societal progress.

questions.question: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in the state of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hornbill Festival is an annual cultural festival celebrated in the state of **Nagaland, India**.
 
• It is organized by the Government of Nagaland to promote the rich cultural heritage of the 16 major tribes and sub-tribes of the state.
 
• The festival is named after the **Hornbill bird**, which is considered a symbol of respect and folklore in Naga culture.
 
• It is celebrated **from December 1 to 10** every year at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, near Kohima, the capital of Nagaland.
 
• The festival includes cultural performances, traditional music, dance, food, crafts, and a variety of events like the Hornbill International Rock Contest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagaland:**

 
 
• Nagaland is located in the northeastern region of India and shares its borders with Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, and Manipur, as well as Myanmar.
 
• The state is known for its diverse tribes, each having its own unique traditions, language, and festivals.
 
 
 
• **Hornbill Bird:**
 
 
• The Hornbill bird is a large, colorful bird found in the tropical and subtropical regions of Asia and Africa.
 
• It holds a significant place in Naga folklore and symbolizes the rich biodiversity of the region.
 
 
 
• **Tourism Impact:**
 
 
• The Hornbill Festival attracts both domestic and international tourists, boosting the local economy and promoting cultural exchange.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Festival of Festivals" and serves as a platform for showcasing the state’s cultural vibrancy.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage:**
 
 
• Festivals like the Hornbill Festival contribute to the preservation of intangible cultural heritage, which is recognized as vital by UNESCO.

questions.question: Which of the following subjects comes under the Concurrent List?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newspapers**__**. link**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution includes subjects on which both the Centre and States can legislate.
 
• **Newspapers** is included in the Concurrent List as per Schedule VII of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Subjects like Newspapers, forests, marriage, and adoption often require coordination between the Centre and States.
 
• Legislation by States on Concurrent List subjects is valid unless it conflicts with a central law, in which case the central law prevails.
 
• The Concurrent List comprises **52 items**, and fisheries is one among them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Schedule VII of the Indian Constitution**:

 
 
• It divides legislative powers between the Union and States into three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
• The Union List contains subjects like defense, foreign affairs, and atomic energy, which are exclusively legislated by the Centre.
 
• The State List includes subjects like police, public health, and agriculture, primarily legislated by the States.
 
• The Concurrent List contains subjects like education, forest, and fisheries that require joint effort by the Centre and States.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Process on Concurrent Subjects**:
 
 
• Both the Centre and States can legislate on subjects in the Concurrent List.
 
• If there is a conflict between a state law and a central law, the law enacted by the Centre prevails.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Concurrent List Subjects**:
 
 
• Education, electricity, and criminal law are notable subjects under the Concurrent List.
 
• Subjects like marriage and adoption require harmonized legislation between States and the Centre.

questions.question: Which law of thermodynamics states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or converted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First Law of Thermodynamics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **First Law of Thermodynamics** states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another or transferred between systems.
 
• This law is also known as the **Law of Energy Conservation**.
 
• The mathematical expression of the First Law is: **ΔU = Q - W**, where ΔU is the change in internal energy, Q is the heat added to the system, and W is the work done by the system.
 
• It establishes the principle that the total energy of an isolated system remains constant over time.
 
• The First Law applies universally to all physical and chemical processes, from engines to biological systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics**: Defines thermal equilibrium and forms the basis for the measurement of temperature.
 
• **Second Law of Thermodynamics**: States that the total entropy of an isolated system can never decrease over time and explains the concept of irreversibility in natural processes.
 
• **Third Law of Thermodynamics**: States that as the temperature of a system approaches absolute zero, the entropy of the system approaches a constant minimum.
 
• **Energy Transformation**: Common examples include the conversion of chemical energy to mechanical energy in engines or electrical energy to light energy in bulbs.
 
• **Applications**: The First Law is critical in understanding processes like heat engines, refrigerators, and biological metabolism.

questions.question: Which dancer founded the Kalakshetra Institute in Chennai that promotes performing art forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rukmini Devi Arundale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale** was a renowned Indian classical dancer and the founder of the **Kalakshetra Foundation**, an academy for Bharatanatyam and other Indian art forms.
 
• She was instrumental in reviving and re-establishing Bharatanatyam as a respected and sophisticated classical dance form in the 20th century.
 
• The **Kalakshetra Foundation**, established in 1936 in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, continues to promote Indian performing arts and cultural traditions globally.
 
• She is widely credited with introducing innovative techniques in stagecraft and costumes to enhance the visual appeal of Bharatanatyam.
 
• Rukmini Devi also worked towards preserving Indian heritage and was a strong advocate of cultural education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• It combines expressions (bhava), melody (raga), rhythm (tala), and dramatic performance (natya).
 
• This dance form was traditionally performed in temples as an offering to deities.
 
 
 
• **Kalakshetra Foundation:**
 
 
• Kalakshetra means "a holy place of arts" and focuses on Bharatanatyam, Carnatic music, and visual arts.
 
• The foundation is recognized as an institution of national importance under the Indian Constitution.
 
• It follows a Gurukula system of education, emphasizing discipline and holistic learning.
 
 
 
• **Rukmini Devi's Contributions:**
 
 
• She redefined Bharatanatyam by removing its association with Devadasi culture and aligning it with modern aesthetics.
 
• She introduced mythological themes and used Sanskrit compositions in performances.
 
• Her efforts ensured the survival and global recognition of Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **Honors and Recognition:**
 
 
• Rukmini Devi was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 1952 for her contributions to Indian culture.
 
• She received the Padma Bhushan in 1956 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 1967.

questions.question: When did the Indian Census start?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1872**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first Indian Census was conducted in **1872** during the period of British rule.
 
• It was conducted under the authority of **Lord Mayo**, the then Viceroy of India.
 
• This census was not synchronous, meaning it was conducted in different regions at different times between 1865 and 1872.
 
• It aimed to collect demographic data such as population size, caste, religion, occupation, and literacy levels.
 
• It laid the foundation for a systematic decadal (every 10 years) census, which officially began in **1881**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decadal Census:** The Indian Census became a regular decadal exercise starting from 1881 and has continued ever since, except for disruptions during major events like the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• **Registrar General and Census Commissioner:** The office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, is responsible for conducting the census.
 
• **Modern Census Features:** The modern Indian Census collects data on population, economic activity, literacy, housing, amenities, and migration, among other things.
 
• **2011 Census:** The most recent completed census was in 2011, which recorded India’s population at 1.21 billion, making it the second-most populous country in the world.
 
• **Digital Census:** The upcoming census is expected to incorporate digital technology for data collection, marking a significant shift from traditional paper-based methods.

questions.question: According to Köppen's climate classification scheme, which letter represents Warm Temperate climate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Köppen's climate classification** is one of the most widely used systems for categorizing the world's climates based on temperature and precipitation patterns.
 
• The letter **C** in Köppen's classification represents **Warm Temperate climates**, also known as "Mesothermal climates."
 
• Warm Temperate climates (C) are characterized by **moderate temperatures**, no extreme cold or heat, and distinct seasonal variations.
 
• Regions with "C" climates typically experience **wet winters** and **dry summers**, often associated with Mediterranean climates.
 
• Examples of areas with Warm Temperate climates include the **Mediterranean Basin, parts of California, and southern Australia.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Köppen Climate Classification System:**

 
 
• Developed by **Vladimir Köppen**, this system categorizes climates into five primary groups: A (Tropical), B (Dry), C (Warm Temperate), D (Cold), and E (Polar).
 
• Each group is further divided based on seasonal precipitation and temperature patterns.
 
 
 
• **Mesothermal Climate:**
 
 
• Mesothermal climates (C) are defined by moderate temperatures and sufficient precipitation to sustain vegetation throughout the year.
 
• They are typically located in mid-latitude regions, between tropical and polar zones.
 
 
 
• **Subcategories of "C" climates:**
 
 
• Csa - Mediterranean climate (hot summers, wet winters).
 
• Cfa - Humid subtropical climate (hot summers, consistent rainfall).
 
• Cfb - Marine west coast climate (cool summers, mild winters).
 
 
 
• **Importance of Climate Classification:**
 
 
• Helps scientists understand and predict global climate patterns.
 
• Supports agricultural planning and environmental conservation efforts.

questions.question: Which of the following periods does the Iron Age in India encompass?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1500 BCE - 200 CE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Iron Age in India is marked by the widespread use of iron tools and weapons, which significantly contributed to advancements in agriculture and warfare.
 
• It is estimated to have begun around **1500 BCE**, overlapping with the later Vedic period and extending up to approximately **200 CE**.
 
• This period saw the emergence of regional kingdoms, the rise of urban centers, and the evolution of early state formations.
 
• Archaeological evidence such as iron artifacts, tools, and megalithic structures found in South India and other regions supports the timeline of the Iron Age in India.
 
• Important cultural advancements during this era include the development of iron metallurgy and its influence on socio-economic transformations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Metallurgy:** Iron processing techniques were refined during this period, leading to the production of stronger tools and weapons compared to earlier materials like copper and bronze.
 
• **Megalithic Culture:** The Iron Age coincided with the spread of megalithic burial practices, particularly in South India, which are characterized by large stone structures used as burial sites.
 
• **Vedic Literature:** The later Vedic texts, such as the Brahmanas and Upanishads, provide insights into the socio-political and religious developments of the Iron Age.
 
• **Urbanization:** The Iron Age laid the foundation for urbanization and trade networks in northern and central India, paving the way for the emergence of cities like Kashi and Hastinapur.
 
• **Regional Variations:** While the northern regions of India developed iron tools for agriculture and warfare, the southern regions showcased distinct megalithic traditions and localized advancements.
